cls: Selective prostacyclin (IP) receptor agonist - oral pulmonary vasodilator
pharm: Selexipag and its active metabolite selectively agonize the prostacyclin (IP) receptor (distinct from prostacyclin analogs), causing vasodilation of the pulmonary arterial bed and inhibition of pulmonary vascular smooth-muscle proliferation, reducing pulmonary vascular resistance in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
quick: Start 200 mcg twice daily; titrate weekly by 200 mcg to highest tolerated, max 1600 mcg BID
May be taken with or without food; with food may improve tolerability
Limited data; use only if clearly needed (PAH itself is high-risk in pregnancy)
Avoid breastfeeding during treatment (excretion in animal milk)
No adjustment for mild-moderate; not studied in severe (eGFR <15) / dialysis
Moderate impairment (Child-Pugh B): once-daily dosing; severe (C): not recommended
PAH symptoms/functional class, thyroid function, blood pressure, tolerability
summary: Selexipag is an orally available, selective agonist of the prostacyclin (IP) receptor, indicated for the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1) to delay disease progression and reduce the risk of hospitalization for PAH. Although it targets the same receptor as prostacyclin, it is chemically distinct from prostacyclin and its analogs and is highly selective for the IP receptor over other prostanoid receptors. It is FDA-approved. Treatment begins at 200 mcg twice daily and is individually up-titrated, usually in weekly 200-mcg increments, to the highest tolerated dose up to 1600 mcg twice daily; dose-limiting effects are pharmacologic prostacyclin-type symptoms (headache, flushing, jaw pain, diarrhea, nausea, myalgia, extremity pain). Strong CYP2C8 inhibitors (e.g., gemfibrozil) markedly increase exposure and are contraindicated. Hepatic impairment requires dose-frequency reduction.
indications: Treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1) in adults to delay disease progression and reduce the risk of hospitalization for PAH

Efficacy established predominantly in patients with WHO functional class II-III, including idiopathic/heritable PAH, PAH associated with connective tissue disease, and PAH associated with congenital heart disease

dosage.d: Increase by 200 mcg twice daily at weekly intervals to the highest tolerated dose
dosage.n: Maximum 1600 mcg twice daily; the individualized maintenance dose is the highest tolerated

dosage.d: Reduce by 200 mcg twice daily if a dose is not tolerated
dosage.n: Do not discontinue abruptly without considering down-titration

dosage.d: Start 200 mcg ONCE daily; increase by 200 mcg once daily weekly as tolerated

admin: Take twice daily (morning and evening), with or without food; taking with food may improve tolerability
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not split, crush, or chew
Begin at 200 mcg twice daily and increase in 200-mcg twice-daily steps at weekly intervals as tolerated
If intolerable prostacyclin-type effects occur, reduce by one step rather than stopping abruptly
If 3 or more consecutive doses are missed, re-titrate the dose; counsel patients not to stop abruptly
moa: Selexipag is a selective agonist of the prostacyclin (IP, prostaglandin I2) receptor. It is hydrolyzed to its pharmacologically active metabolite (ACT-333679), which is more potent than the parent and is also IP-selective. Agonism of the IP receptor on pulmonary arterial smooth muscle increases intracellular cyclic AMP, producing vasodilation of the pulmonary vasculature, and exerts antiproliferative and antiplatelet effects. Unlike prostacyclin analogs, selexipag is structurally distinct and selective for the IP receptor over other prostanoid (EP, DP, FP, TP) receptors, which may favorably influence tolerability. The net effect is reduced pulmonary vascular resistance and improved pulmonary hemodynamics in PAH.

absolute: Concomitant use of strong CYP2C8 inhibitors (e.g., gemfibrozil) - approximately doubles parent and increases active metabolite exposure
Known hypersensitivity to selexipag or excipients
relative: Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (pulmonary edema risk with vasodilators)
Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) - not recommended
Concomitant moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors (reduce to once daily)
Hyperthyroidism / hyperthyroidism risk (thyroid function abnormalities reported)
monitor: PAH symptoms, WHO functional class, and exercise capacity
Thyroid function tests as clinically indicated

preg: There are limited data on selexipag use in pregnant women. PAH can worsen during pregnancy and is associated with high maternal mortality. Use only if clearly needed after weighing maternal and fetal risks; discuss PAH-pregnancy risks with the patient.
lact: There are no data on selexipag in human milk. Selexipag and its metabolite were present in the milk of lactating rats. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for mild or moderate renal impairment. Use caution in severe renal impairment (eGFR 15 to <30 mL/min/1.73 m2). There is no experience in patients on dialysis or with eGFR <15.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed in mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A). In moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B), use once-daily dosing. Selexipag is not recommended in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C).

major: Strong CYP2C8 inhibitors (gemfibrozil) - contraindicated; substantially increase exposure to selexipag and its active metabolite
Strong CYP2C8 inducers (rifampicin) - reduce active metabolite exposure; may require dose increase and re-adjustment when stopped
moderate: Moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors (e.g., clopidogrel) - increase exposure; reduce selexipag to once-daily dosing
Other pulmonary vasodilators / antihypertensives - additive hypotensive effect
minor: No clinically significant interaction with warfarin, midazolam, or hormonal contraceptives
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food may improve gastrointestinal tolerability and slightly delays absorption.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause thyroid function abnormalities (decreased TSH); monitor thyroid tests as indicated.

serious: Pulmonary edema (especially if underlying pulmonary veno-occlusive disease)
emergency: Acute pulmonary edema (suggesting pulmonary veno-occlusive disease)

monitoring: PAH symptoms, WHO functional class, and 6-minute walk distance
Thyroid function tests when clinically indicated
Tolerability and need for dose adjustment during up-titration
counsel: Take twice a day, with or without food; food may help reduce stomach upset
Your dose will be increased step by step each week - some side effects like headache, flushing, jaw pain, diarrhea, and muscle aches are common and often improve as your body adjusts
Do not stop the medicine suddenly; if you miss three or more doses in a row, contact your doctor as the dose may need to be re-started lower
Tell your doctor about all your medicines - some (like the cholesterol drug gemfibrozil) cannot be taken with selexipag
Report severe or persistent diarrhea, fainting, or worsening breathlessness
Keep all follow-up appointments to track your pulmonary hypertension
pk: Active metabolite drives effect; clinical benefit assessed over weeks of titration
Selexipag Tmax ~1-3 h; active metabolite Tmax ~3-4 h
Twice-daily dosing maintains effect (once-daily in hepatic/CYP2C8-inhibitor situations)
pearls: Selectively agonizes the prostacyclin IP receptor but is chemically distinct from prostacyclin analogs (not a prostanoid); IS FDA-approved
Dose is individually up-titrated weekly to the highest tolerated level (max 1600 mcg BID) - the maintenance dose differs between patients
Strong CYP2C8 inhibitor gemfibrozil is CONTRAINDICATED; moderate inhibitor clopidogrel requires once-daily dosing
Prostacyclin-type side effects (headache, jaw pain, flushing, diarrhea, myalgia) are common and often dose-limiting
Do not stop abruptly; missing >=3 consecutive doses requires re-titration
Watch for pulmonary edema - may indicate underlying pulmonary veno-occlusive disease
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day, then resume your usual schedule; do not take two doses at the same time. If you miss doses for 3 or more days in a row, contact your doctor, as the medicine may need to be re-started at a lower dose and titrated up again.
overdose: There is limited experience with overdose. Isolated reports describe nausea, vomiting, and transient hypotension. There is no specific antidote. Manage with supportive measures and monitoring of cardiovascular status; selexipag is highly protein bound, so dialysis is unlikely to be effective.
